findings.title: All 12 success criteria are covered by traceable, correctly sequenced tasks
findings.description: Verified criterion-by-criterion: SC1 → 1.1/1.2/8.5 (selector incl. `candidates` unrecognized); SC2 → 5.1/5.2/5.3 (verbatim questions, once-as-one-block timing, defect rule, inventory check) plus 8.1's "nothing else asked" check; SC3 → 3.1/3.2/3.3 (attribution rules, closed checklist, absence-is-observation) plus 4.1's mapping table and 8.1's document checks; SC4 → 4.1/4.2 (dropped-topics rule in skill text); SC5 → 5.1 (skip semantics) + 8.2 (decline-path walkthrough); SC6 → 6.1/6.2/6.3 + 8.1 (verbatim diff) + 8.4 (re-run, byte-identity via `git diff`); SC7 → 2.1 (terminal precondition), 6.1 (both contract checks with distinct stop messages), 8.3 (loud stop, nothing written); SC8 → 6.2 + 8.4 (default stop, augment refillability); SC9 → 7.2 + 8.1 (`cf validate frontmatter`, `squadron` filename, divergence stated and recorded); SC10 → 7.1/7.3 (checkable rule, full outcome set, no invented outcomes) + 8.1 provenance lines; SC11 → 3.1 read discipline + 8.6 (jq-only reads, no function/class nodes, `git diff --name-only` changed-file set, empty `src/` diff); SC12 → 8.1 (PM live, deliberate correction outcome) + 9.3 hand-off. Sequencing is linear and dependency-correct: each verify subtask (1.2, 2.2, 3.4, 4.2, 5.3, 6.3) immediately follows its authoring subtask, 8.4 correctly depends on 8.1's document, and the PM-live 8.1 carries the framing notice. No circular dependencies. Task sizes (1/5–3/5) are appropriate; 8.1 is the largest but is a bounded checklist with explicit PM framing, not an oversized task. No scope creep found: 7.4 (362 cross-reference sentence) traces to Implementation Notes; 8.6's ruff/pytest checks trace to SC11 ("no incidental change"), not new scope.

findings.title: SC4's document-level clause is not re-verified on the generated concept
findings.description: Success Criterion 4 requires dropped topics (why-now, audience evolution, methodology preference) to "appear nowhere **in the document** — neither as content nor as gap markers." Task 4.1/4.2 verify the rule is authored in and verified within the skill text, and 8.1 verifies interaction-level behavior ("nothing else asked"), but Task 8.1's checklist for the written `000-concept.squadron.md` contains no check that the dropped topics are absent from the generated document itself (e.g., grep for why-now/audience/methodology gap markers or headings). The design's own walkthrough omits this too, so the task file is faithful to the design — but the walkthrough is the only place the output document is inspected, so a hallucinated "why now?" gap marker would pass uncaught. Suggested fix: add one line to 8.1's document checklist confirming the three topics appear nowhere in the written concept, as content or as `[GAP: ...]`.

findings.title: Commit markers use checkbox items and bare `Commit:` rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: All eight commit markers (lines 99, 125, 164, 185, 221, 254, 296, 351) are written as `- [ ] Commit: \`feat: ...\`` checklist items. Their *placement* is correct per the review convention: each sits after its task's verification subtask at a working, tested point (selector after 1.2, sources after 3.4, etc.), there is no marker after every task (Tasks 0 and 9.x have none — 9.3 commits in prose), and none sits only at the end. The format deviates from the plain-line `**Commit**:` convention, but CLAUDE.md's document conventions mandate "`[ ]` checkbox" for "each item and subitem" in task files, so the checkbox form is defensible under project convention. Noting for consistency; no action required unless the project wants to resolve the convention conflict.

findings.title: No load-test or CI-gating obligations apply to this slice
findings.description: The design restates no NFR (no performance/load requirements; it is a markdown-only skill-flow slice), so no `tests/load/` task is required, and consequently no CI wiring task is needed. Single task file, 9 tasks / 22 subitems — proportionate to the design's 3/5 relative effort and "everything is markdown editing" scope.
